success_patterns: In clues describing a work (film, book, series, band) with several named anchors (actor, year, network, song titles), the agent picked the title that recurs across most passages together with all the anchors (Thunder Road, In the Heat of the Night, Counting Crows, Funny Girl). It gave the bare title with no 'film', 'series' or 'group' descriptor.

For a clue with one quoted word of a title ('this "Express"'), the agent answered the FULL standard title ('The Polar Express'), not just the missing words. The quoted word is part of the answer, not a separate modifier to strike.
The agent honored the exact part requested ('Last name of the French brothers' -> 'Michelin'), not a full name or a company description.
For a bare 'YEAR: role/descriptor' fragment ('1968:Starring Barbra Streisand'), the agent answered with the work, not the person or the year.

When the clue was a near-copy of a sentence repeated across passages with one slot blanked (mistletoe 'held magic powers to bestow life and fertility'), the agent filled the slot with the repeated word. Where an archive hit reproduced the clue, it stayed on the matching entity.

patch.reasoning: All eight successes were plain applications of Rule 3 and Rule 2, which are already covered. Two successes sit in tension with existing wording. 'The Polar Express' for 'this "Express"' could be wrongly cut by the delete-clue-words test and the 'give only the MISSING part' rule. 'Michelin' for 'Last name of...' conflicts with the blanket first+last person-name rule. A short clarification for each protects these passes. A one-line example of the 'year + descriptor -> work' pattern reinforces Rule 1 without adding a new section.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - QUOTED TITLE FRAGMENT: when the clue puts a single word of a work's title in quotes and asks for the work ('about this "Express"', 'this "...Road"'), the quoted word is PART of the answer. Give the full standard title as the passages repeat it ('The Polar Express'). The delete-clue-words test applies to separate modifiers (a descriptor like 'hasty' before 'dessert'), not to a quoted word that is the tail of a title.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - PART-OF-NAME REQUESTS: when the clue asks for only a part ('Last name of the French brothers who...', 'first name of...', 'surname'), answer with exactly that part ('Michelin'). The full-name rule in the strategic block applies only when the clue asks for the person.

edits.target: ## Rule 1: Questions are Jeopardy-style clues; always answer with the missing entity
edits.content: - A bare 'YEAR: descriptor' fragment ('1968:Starring Barbra Streisand') or a clue naming a star, network and year ('Carroll O'Connor stars as chief Bill Gillespie in this NBC series based on 1967's Best Picture') asks for the WORK (film, series, song) that the passages repeatedly tie to all those anchors. Give the bare title ('Funny Girl', 'In the Heat of the Night'), not the star, year or a label like 'film'.
